item.title: FreeBSD exec_args_adjust_args() Out-of-Bounds memmove — Local Privilege Escalation via sshd Race (CVE-2026-7270)
item.description:

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System FreeBSD kernel — sys/kern/kern_exec.c exec_args_adjust_args()
Versions Affected FreeBSD 11.0 through 14.4 (all releases at time of disclosure)

Summary

An operator-precedence bug in FreeBSD’s exec_args_adjust_args() (present since 2013) computes a memmove size using + consume instead of - consume, causing the copy length to be roughly double the correct value. With a ~265KB argv[0] supplied via a shebang exec, the resulting memmove overflows the exec_map entry by ~2KB into an adjacent entry with no crash or fault. By racing this overflow against sshd’s fork/execv on incoming connections, the exploit plants an LD_PRELOAD reference in sshd-session’s exec_map entry; since sshd-session runs root-to-root with no suid/sgid transition, the runtime linker honors LD_PRELOAD, and the attacker’s shared object constructor executes as uid 0, dropping a setuid-root shell.
